analysis.one_liner: Adani Green Energy builds, owns and operates solar, wind and hybrid power plants across India, selling electricity under long-term (often 25-year) contracts to state utilities and other buyers.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 (July-Sept 2026) results came on Oct 21, 2026: consolidated net profit rose 16% year-on-year to ₹747 crore and EBITDA jumped 51% to ₹3,835 crore on a ~92-93% EBITDA margin, as operational capacity grew 24% YoY to 20,763 MW. The stock still fell on results day amid concern over rising debt. An EGM on Nov 16, 2026 will ask shareholders to raise the company's borrowing cap from ₹25,000 crore to ₹40,000 crore and approve ~₹5,900 crore of related-party purchases (turbines, solar modules) from group entities Adani New Industries and Mundra Solar Energy.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a capital-intensive, debt-funded business: it borrows heavily to build power plants, then collects steady contracted revenue for decades. Revenue and operating profit (EBITDA) are growing fast as new capacity switches on, but net profit is still thin because depreciation and interest on all that debt eat into it. The stock trades at a very high earnings multiple because investors are pricing in years of future capacity growth, not today's actual profit - and the company is now asking to borrow even more to keep building.
analysis.quarters: Revenue/EBITDA growth has been consistently strong: Q2 FY27 revenue rose roughly 39-45% (reports vary on the exact base) to about ₹4,500-4,900 crore, EBITDA grew faster (+51% to ₹3,835 crore) on margin expansion to ~92-93%, and consolidated net profit rose 16% to ₹747 crore - this is the figure that a cluster of independent outlets (Business Standard, Free Press Journal, Newsbytes) converge on; one outlier report cited ₹673 crore/+15%, which was set aside as inconsistent with the majority. Separately, the standalone (parent-only) profit fell 93% to ₹33 crore - not a red flag, just a reflection that nearly all earnings sit inside project-level subsidiaries, not the holding company. Management's emphasis on the call was capacity additions (4,083 MW added in H1 FY27) and battery storage scale-up, not profit per se.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is 60.1% below its April 2022 peak (₹2,970.5 vs ₹1,185.1 now), and there is no split or demerger in the data to explain this away - it is a genuine, large loss of capital for anyone who bought near the top. The fall tracks two specific overhangs: the January 2023 Hindenburg short-seller report and the November 2024 US DOJ/SEC indictment that was centred specifically on Adani Green's solar supply contracts. Both have since eased - the DOJ criminal case was dismissed in August 2026 and the SEC matter was settled via consent judgment in May 2026 (alongside a reported $10 billion investment pledge by the promoter) - and the stock has recovered some ground, up 13.44% over the past year even as the Nifty fell 12.71% and peer NTPC Green fell 19.42%. But over 5 years the stock is still down 1.44% while the Nifty gained 24.69%, so long-term holders have badly lagged the market despite the growth narrative.
analysis.valuation_read: P/E estimates across data providers range roughly 110-134x and P/B around 9.9-10.7x, both far above a sector median P/E near 24x and P/B near 2.2x. It is expensive mainly because net profit is still small relative to the asset base: most capacity is recently built, so depreciation and interest charges are high even though the underlying power-generation economics (93% EBITDA margin) are strong. Whether that multiple is justified depends entirely on whether the committed expansion pipeline gets built on time and the mounting debt gets serviced without dilution or distress - that is a forward bet, not something verifiable from current numbers.
analysis.growth_read: This is volume-led growth, not margin engineering: operational capacity rose 24% YoY to 20,763 MW, with 4,083 MW of new greenfield capacity added in H1 FY27 alone, and capex is rising in step (₹17,160 crore in H1, up 38% YoY). The margin expansion to ~92-93% EBITDA is partly a genuine operating-leverage effect and partly a mix shift toward higher-margin battery storage (BESS capacity more than doubled from 3.55 GWh to 6.63 GWh since June 2026) - worth watching rather than assuming it simply continues.
analysis.health_read: At the EBITDA line the business converts revenue into cash well (margins near 90%+), and net profit is positive and growing (+16% YoY). But the balance sheet carries heavy leverage: gross debt rose from ₹100,164 crore (Mar-26) to ₹114,848 crore (Sep-26) and net debt from ₹91,252 crore to ₹102,973 crore in just six months, with net debt/run-rate EBITDA holding around 5.6x per management and debt-to-equity near 5.2x. The main risk here is financial (interest cost, refinancing and the ability to keep raising the ₹40,000 crore borrowing cap being sought), not the operating business itself, which is cash-generative on a per-project basis.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters hold 62.43% with 0.00% pledged as of September 2026, and the group has formally declared no new share encumbrances for FY26 - clean on pledging. Institutional ownership looks thin on the domestic side: FII holding is about 11.33% but DII holding is reported at 0%, and GQG Partners - the high-profile global investor that backed Adani stocks in 2023 - has been trimming its Adani Green stake through 2026, down to roughly the 3-4.5% range from higher levels earlier in the year (sources differ slightly on the exact percentage). There is no indication of a large, new marquee institutional buyer stepping in to replace that reduced exposure.
strengths: EBITDA margin near 92-93% in Q2/H1 FY27, reflecting long-term contracted tariffs rather than spot pricing risk
Operational capacity up 24% YoY to 20,763 MW, with 4,083 MW added in H1 FY27 alone - real, executed growth, not just announced plans
Promoter pledge at 0% with a formal no-new-encumbrance declaration for FY26

The US DOJ criminal case (dismissed Aug 2026) and SEC civil case (settled by consent, May 2026) that were specifically tied to Adani Green's solar contracts have been resolved, removing a multi-year company-specific legal overhang
watchpoints: Net debt jumped from ₹91,252 crore to ₹102,973 crore in just six months (Mar-26 to Sep-26), and the Nov 16, 2026 EGM seeks to raise the borrowing cap from ₹25,000 crore to ₹40,000 crore
A P/E of roughly 110-130x prices in years of flawless capacity execution; any delay, tariff dispute, or offtake renegotiation would hit the multiple hard
Zero reported DII ownership and a global anchor investor (GQG Partners) trimming its position through 2026 suggest some institutional caution persists even after the legal overhang eased

~₹5,900 crore of related-party procurement (Adani New Industries, Mundra Solar Energy) is up for shareholder approval at the same EGM - routine for a vertically integrated group, but worth tracking given the group's governance history
analysis.one_thing: Whether net debt/EBITDA (currently cited by management around 5.6x and rising in absolute rupee terms) stabilizes or climbs further once the proposed ₹40,000 crore borrowing cap is drawn down - that will show whether the current expansion is increasingly funded by fresh debt rather than internal cash generation.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 consolidated net profit (₹747 crore, +16% YoY) and EBITDA (₹3,835 crore, +51%) were cross-checked across multiple independent outlets (Business Standard, Free Press Journal, Newsbytes, eqmagpro); one outlier figure (₹673 crore/+15%, BusinessToday/indmoney) did not match this cluster and was set aside rather than averaged in. P/E and P/B figures varied by 10-20% across data providers (anandrathi, valueresearch, venturasecurities), so a range is given rather than a single point estimate. The exact DII/FII/MF shareholding breakdown and precise GQG Partners stake could not be pinned to a single consistent figure across sources - recommend confirming current shareholding pattern directly on Screener or the BSE/NSE filing before relying on exact percentages. Promoter pledge, debt and capacity figures reconcile closely across the company's own H1 FY27 investor-update coverage.
